english_meaning: The One Who acts in a good and fine manner
bahasa_meaning: Yang Maha Berbuat Kebaikan dan Ihsan
proof_hadith: At-Tabaraanee. Classified as saheeh 'authentic' by Sheikh Al-Albaanee
proof_text: …Allah is the Doer of Good and He loves [to see His slaves] do good.
aqeedah_belief: Believing in Al-Muhsin means affirming this Name as established in the Prophetic Sunnah—graded sahih by Al-Albani in Al-Jami' al-Saghir 1824 and hasan in Al-Sahihah 470—while recognizing its verbal occurrences in the Qur'an, such as Quran 28:77, Quran 12:100, and Quran 32:7. As Al-Raghib, Al-Qurtubi, and Al-Munawi explain, it commits the believer to certainty that Allah's beneficence is an inseparable attribute that exceeds mere justice by giving more than what is owed, manifested in both the perfection of His creation and His Islamic legislation (Quran 5:50). As Ibn al-Qayyim explains, knowing that none surpasses Al-Muhsin in perfection and goodness anchors the heart in supreme love and hope toward Him.
dua_usage: Practice *Ihsan* (excellence) in worship and dealings.
when_to_invoke: Practice *Ihsan* (excellence) in worship and dealings.
description_en: Al-Muhsin is the One who unites boundless beneficence toward creation with supreme excellence in all His actions, sustaining and guiding everything He has made. As Al-Munawi explains, no existing creature can do without His beneficence for even the blink of an eye, as every being depends on Him for both its initial existence and its continuous support.
description_ms: Al-Muhsin ialah Tuhan yang menggabungkan limpahan ihsan kepada makhluk dengan kesempurnaan dalam setiap perbuatan-Nya, serta memelihara dan membimbing segala ciptaan-Nya. Seperti yang dijelaskan oleh Al-Munawi, tiada suatu makhluk pun yang terlepas daripada ihsan-Nya walau sekelip mata, kerana setiap kewujudan bergantung pada nikmat penciptaan dan bantuan-Nya yang berterusan.
source_reference: Shaykh Uthaymeen list-of-the-99-names-of-allaah-shaykh-uthaymeen-dawud-burbank.pdf; Booklet en_The_Beautiful_Names_of_Allah.pdf p.149; Comprehensive MD Divine Names_ A Comprehensive Guide to the 99 Attributes.md
al_jalil_commentary: Belief in Al-Muhsin (The Beneficent) motivates one to adorn themselves with the quality of Ihsan (excellence, beneficence), as Allah is Muhsin and loves the Muhsinin. Ihsan for the servant has two aspects: Ihsan in the worship of Allah, which is to worship Him as if you see Him; and Ihsan towards the creation, by delivering all kinds of good to them.

proof_text: …Allah is the Giver and I am Al-Qaasim (i.e. the distributor) …
aqeedah_belief: Believing in Al-Mu'tee means affirming this Name as established in Sahih al-Bukhari 3116 and in its Qur'anic verbal and nominal forms in Quran 17:20, Quran 93:5, and Quran 108:1. As Ibn al-Qayyim explains regarding Sahih al-Bukhari 844 and Sahih Muslim 593, it commits the believer to certainty that Allah alone possesses the reality of giving and withholding without partner, and that complete servitude pairs belief in Al-Mu'tee with belief in Al-Mani' since His giving by mercy and withholding by wisdom both flow from His authority. As Al-Jalil explains in connection with Quran 17:20-21, Al-Mu'tee extends His worldly gifts to both believers and disbelievers alike while reserving His eternal bounty in the Hereafter exclusively for the believers.
dua_usage: Call upon Al-Mu'tee alone to bring benefits and repel harms without attaching your heart to created intermediaries, eagerly asking Him above all for the imperishable gift of Paradise, its bliss, and the vision of Allah.
when_to_invoke: Reach for Al-Mu'tee when seeking any benefit or protection from harm in which created beings seem to hold the outcome, remembering as Al-Jalil explains that weak creatures possess nothing unless the True Giver permits and makes them a means for the gift.
description_en: Al-Mu'tee is the True Giver whose unrestricted giving encompasses every gift—above all faith and guidance—and who never grows weary of bestowing upon His servants. As Ibn al-Qayyim explains, He is Al-Mu'tee first and last because He alone grants both the ability to do good and the reward for it, and giving is dearer to Him than withholding.
description_ms: Al-Mu'tee ialah Tuhan Yang Maha Memberi secara hakiki yang kurniaan-Nya meliputi setiap pemberian—terutamanya iman dan hidayah—serta tidak pernah jemu memberi kepada hamba-hamba-Nya. Seperti yang dijelaskan oleh Ibn al-Qayyim, Dialah Al-Mu'tee pada awal dan akhir kerana Dia sahaja yang mengurniakan taufik untuk beramal serta ganjarannya, malah memberi lebih dicintai-Nya daripada menahan.
source_reference: Shaykh Uthaymeen list-of-the-99-names-of-allaah-shaykh-uthaymeen-dawud-burbank.pdf; Booklet en_The_Beautiful_Names_of_Allah.pdf p.165; Comprehensive MD Divine Names_ A Comprehensive Guide to the 99 Attributes.md
al_jalil_commentary: Understanding that Allah is the true Giver leads to directing all requests for benefit and protection from harm to Him alone, as no created being can give or withhold anything without His permission. It also inspires the believer to be generous with what Allah has given them.

proof_hadith: Reported by At-Tirmidhee and Abu Daawood
proof_text: O Allah! I ask You by virtue of the fact that all praise is due to You; none has the right to be worshiped but You, the Bestower…
aqeedah_belief: Believing in Al-Mannaan means affirming this Name from the Sunnah—graded sahih by Al-Albani in Sahih at-Tirmidhi 2763—and holding, as Al-Qurtubi explains, that it encompasses both Allah's attribute of action in pouring forth gifts and His attribute of speech in recounting His favors upon creation. As Ibn al-Qayyim establishes against the Qadariyyah regarding Quran 95:6, Quran 49:17, Sahih al-Bukhari 5673, and Sahih Muslim 2817, the believer affirms that faith, obedience, and entry into Paradise are purely by Allah's unmerited grace rather than a price paid by human deeds. Witnessing Al-Mannaan alongside Al-Awwal, as Ibn al-Qayyim states, commits the heart to recognizing the precedence of Allah's favor and the servant's utter poverty before Him.
dua_usage: Call upon Al-Mannaan in du'a as recorded in the supplication of Anas in Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3475 and Sunan Abi Dawud 1493—graded sahih by Al-Albani in Sahih at-Tirmidhi 2763 as invoking Allah's Greatest Name—while recognizing that every blessing in both worlds is sought purely from His unmerited grace.
when_to_invoke: Reach for Al-Mannaan when you feel tempted to rely on worldly causes, credit yourself for your obedience, or remind others of your charity, recalling as Ibn al-Qayyim explains that His preceding grace alone upholds you every moment.
description_en: Al-Mannaan is the Abundant Bestower of unmerited grace who, as Ibn Taymiyyah and Ibn al-Athir explain, generously grants favors before being asked and without seeking any return from creation. As Ibn al-Qayyim explains, unlike human boasting that spoils a gift, Allah's reminding His servants of His favor perfects and sweetens the blessing because every good in both worlds is purely His gift.
description_ms: Al-Mannaan ialah Tuhan Yang Maha Melimpahkan Kurnia yang, seperti dijelaskan oleh Ibn Taymiyyah dan Ibn al-Athir, memberi nikmat dengan murah hati sebelum diminta dan tanpa mengharapkan sebarang balasan daripada makhluk. Seperti yang dijelaskan oleh Ibn al-Qayyim, berbeza dengan ungkitan manusia yang merosakkan pemberian, peringatan Allah tentang kurniaan-Nya menyempurnakan kemanisan nikmat itu kerana setiap kebaikan di dunia dan akhirat adalah semata-mata kurniaan-Nya.
source_reference: Shaykh Uthaymeen list-of-the-99-names-of-allaah-shaykh-uthaymeen-dawud-burbank.pdf; Booklet en_The_Beautiful_Names_of_Allah.pdf p.145; Comprehensive MD Divine Names_ A Comprehensive Guide to the 99 Attributes.md
al_jalil_commentary: Al-Jalil explains that belief in Al-Mannan (The Bestower of Favors) should lead the believer away from the blameworthy trait of reminding others of one's charity to them. Allah has forbidden this among people but has ascribed it to Himself, as His favor is a true endowment and reminder of grace, whereas from humans it is a form of reproach and degradation. Since Allah is the true giver, one should avoid this trait.

english_meaning: The One Who has no partner nor anyone like Him
bahasa_meaning: Yang Maha Tunggal Tiada Sekutu atau Bandingan
proof_text: Surely, Allah is Al-Witr (i.e. One who has no equal), and He likes Al-Witr [prayer].
aqeedah_belief: Believing in Al-Witr—a Name established in the authentic Sunnah rather than the Qur'an (Sahih al-Bukhari 6410; Sahih Muslim 2677)—commits a believer to affirming that Allah is the Unpaired One (Al-Fard) who has no partner or peer, as defined by Al-Khattabi. As Ibn Hajar explains, this Name affirms that Allah is One with no equal in His essence and is entirely free from any division, while also being unique in His names, attributes, and actions. Furthermore, as Ibn al-Qayyim states, affirming that Allah is Al-Witr entails believing that He loves what accords with this attribute, which is why many legislated words and deeds in the Shari'ah are concluded on odd numbers.
salah_usage: Belief in Al-Witr shapes salah by prompting the worshipper to seal their two-by-two night prayers with a single odd-numbered unit of Witr prayer, acting upon the Prophetic instruction recorded in Sunan Abi Dawud 1416 (graded sahih by Al-Albani).
dua_usage: Perform Witr prayers; value uniqueness and Oneness.
dhikr_usage: Penghayatan nama Al-Witr dalam zikir diamalkan dengan mengakhiri bacaan zikir yang disyariatkan pada bilangan ganjil, terutamanya hitungan satu, tiga, atau tujuh kali, sebagaimana yang dihuraikan oleh Al-Jalil.
when_to_invoke: Perform Witr prayers; value uniqueness and Oneness.
description_en: Linguistically denoting an odd, unpaired number, Al-Witr in relation to Allah means the Single One who has no partner, peer, or division in His essence, names, attributes, or actions, as explained by Al-Khattabi and Ibn Hajar. Because Allah is Al-Witr (Sahih al-Bukhari 6410; Sahih Muslim 2677), Ibn al-Qayyim and Al-Jalil note that He loves the quality of odd numbers in worship, reflected in concluding prescribed remembrances and deeds on odd counts such as one, three, or seven.
description_ms: Dari sudut bahasa, Al-Witr bermaksud bilangan ganjil yang tidak berpasangan, manakala bagi Allah ia bermaksud Yang Maha Tunggal yang tiada sekutu, tandingan, atau pembahagian pada zat, nama, sifat, dan perbuatan-Nya seperti yang dijelaskan oleh Al-Khattabi dan Ibn Hajar. Oleh sebab Allah itu Al-Witr (Sahih al-Bukhari 6410; Sahih Muslim 2677), Ibn al-Qayyim dan Al-Jalil menyatakan bahawa Dia menyukai bilangan ganjil dalam ibadah, seperti mengakhiri zikir dan amalan yang disyariatkan pada hitungan satu, tiga, atau tujuh.
source_reference: Shaykh Uthaymeen list-of-the-99-names-of-allaah-shaykh-uthaymeen-dawud-burbank.pdf; Booklet en_The_Beautiful_Names_of_Allah.pdf p.159; Comprehensive MD Divine Names_ A Comprehensive Guide to the 99 Attributes.md
al_jalil_commentary: Since Allah is Al-Witr (The One, The Odd), and He loves the 'witr', a believer should be keen to perform and conclude their sayings and actions with an odd number where prescribed by the Sunnah. This includes the Witr prayer, which concludes the prayers of the night.
dhikr_usage_en: Internalization of the name Al-Witr in dhikr is practiced by concluding prescribed dhikr recitations on an odd number, especially a count of one, three, or seven times, as expounded by Al-Jalil.
dhikr_usage_ms: Penghayatan nama Al-Witr dalam zikir diamalkan dengan mengakhiri bacaan zikir yang disyariatkan pada bilangan ganjil, terutamanya hitungan satu, tiga, atau tujuh kali, sebagaimana yang dihuraikan oleh Al-Jalil.
